correctness.rationale: Every order-five cycle has one 00000 window, so binary DFS with a used-five-factor mask and closure checks enumerates every rotation class exactly once. Independent local-edge-order Euler enumeration over all 2^16 binary choices yields the identical 2048 words. Direct coordinate Hamming counts agree for all 2048*31 shifts with cyclic-bitwise XOR/popcount. The certificate CSV matches full regeneration. The complete histogram is {8:36,10:114,12:1212,14:682,16:4}; adjacent-pair uniformity proves d(1)=16, and all four maximizers match the claimed common correlation profile and one reversal/complement orbit. No infinite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The cyclic shift-distance is a natural signal self-separation / synchronization robustness parameter, equivalent to maximum positive periodic bipolar autocorrelation. Two 2011 primary communications/correlation papers explicitly motivate selecting de Bruijn cycles by autocorrelation. The new full spectrum quantifies all achievable robustness levels among all 2048 order-five cycles, characterizes the rare extremizers (only four, one symmetry orbit), and exhibits the precise negative-sidelobe tradeoff. This is a natural complete finite classification, not an arbitrary subsample or an inference from reproducibility alone.
